title: The Value of Thinking: Learning When to Reason in Hybrid Decision Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.16961v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Existing adaptive-reasoning methods shorten the explicit reasoning a model writes, or skip it by switching modes; either way the answer is still written out token by token. \emph{Rather than deciding how much to think}, we explore a different paradigm, \emph{zero-or-$T$ thinking}: a single model either answers from the implicit thinking inside one forward pass, generating no token, or performs full autoregressive reasoning at a cost of $T$ tokens when that is worth paying. We realise it in a \emph{hybrid decision model} (HDM), where one frozen backbone serves both modes and a lightweight \emph{self-routing block} chooses between them. The block estimates the \emph{value of thinking}, the utility the slow mode is expected to add over the fast one, from what that implicit thinking has already produced, and the slow mode runs only where that value exceeds a price $\lambda$ set per request. translated_title: 思考的价值：在混合决策模型中学习何时进行推理

tldr: 该论文提出“零或T思考”新范式与混合决策模型（HDM）：利用轻量级自路由模块评估显式慢推理相对单次前向内隐思考的“思考价值”，仅当价值超过代价λ时才触发完整的自回归推理，否则零token直接作答。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes the "zero-or-T thinking" paradigm and a Hybrid Decision Model (HDM), where a lightweight self-routing block estimates the "value of thinking" of explicit slow reasoning over implicit single-pass thought, triggering full autoregressive reasoning only when that value exceeds its token cost λ.
